scope: France cast batch 1: seven existing person IDs with accepted C01 holder observations (C01-23 president, C01-37 prime ministers, C01-47 PS first secretaries) and no art for the requested appearance windows, plus one prepared alternate. Each person has one dated, freely licensed likeness photograph copied byte-identical into the repository and one exact prompt. Preparation submitted without generated images. Codex returned seven unchanged PNGs on 2026-10-02; see render-return-batch-01.json. Claude review and runtime registration remain open.
prepared_by: Claude: one preparation agent and one independent verification agent per person, assembled and mechanically corrected by Claude on 2026-10-01. This is not human review, not Codex review and not user approval.

receipts.note: Pinned for completeness; C01-38 (prime ministers 2014-2026) holds no observation of these eight people.

rules: All holder dictionaries below are copied exactly from accepted C01 research (supplements/france.json; identical in france.json). Grouping them under an existing person ID does not promote dates, prove a tenure or extend an office.
Point observations are never expanded to full terms. No start or end is inferred from a successor, election, vote, resignation, farewell or cessation decree; those remain claims.

Requested windows are appearance intervals from the CLAUDE-C06-FRANCE-01 handoff table with exclusive ends. Where a bound comes from party_leaders.json, leadership production or the handoff rather than accepted research, the person entry says so.
Real history stops at 2026-09-07; every window in this batch lies before it.

Image dates describe the source photograph, never the appearance window. Every age gap and every artistic extension (standing body, hands, trousers, shoes, colours added to a black-and-white photograph) is declared in the prompt and here.

Likeness references are dated photographs of the exact person whose licence string, as stated by Commons extmetadata, matches FREE_LICENSES exactly. Original bytes and metadata stay outside Git; the repository copy is byte-identical. Nothing was cropped, edited or labelled; crops happen at registration.

Claude generates, edits and labels no image. Codex renders with its built-in image tool from the exact prompt files and input order in render-request-batch-01.md and returns the unchanged outputs; Claude then performs and records the identity, likeness, era and visual review. The original preparation review flags remain false; the separate render return records actual Codex output inspection, not Claude registration or human acceptance.
Each review batch contains at most ten people.
HTTP response header captures that contain the client IP address or GeoIP cookies are never copied, cited, hashed or committed.

Prompt sha256 values are over the LF bytes committed to Git (equal to `git show HEAD:<path> | sha256sum`). Integration now provides per-file LF checkout rules. Historical CRLF hashes remain diagnostic only.
Birth dates used for age notes are general biographical knowledge, not accepted C01 research.

holder.name: François Mitterrand
holder.note: Observed on 4 January 1990, the first in-text attestation in the period: at their joint press conference at Latché (Élysée archive transcript) Chancellor Kohl says 'Je suis d'accord avec M. Mitterrand' and speaks of working in 1990 with 'le Président de la République'. The Assemblée nationale's record of 27 August 1990 reads his decree of 22 August 1990 and his message of 27 August 1990, both signed FRANÇOIS MITTERRAND.
holder.uncertainty: No start: his second septennat began before the packet period; decision 88-60 PDR of 11 May 1988 ('prendra effet le 21 mai 1988 à 0 heure') and his investiture address of 21 May 1988 are claims on the role, not a holder date, as the Brazil, India and South Africa packets date the holder in office when the period opens by an in-period attestation. No end: no source reviewed states, as a record, the day his functions ended. His letter of 16 May 1995 announces the handover for 'Demain matin à onze heures' (prospective), decision 95-81 PDR gives only the outer limit of 21 May 1995 at 0 heure, his successor's address of 17 May 1995 speaks of the fourteen years 'qui viennent de s'écouler' without a day, and the Council's undated 2012 note dating the 1995 handover to 17 May is retrospective; all are claims, and Jacques Chirac's observation of 17 May 1995 is not used as this end.

supporting_metadata.content: Commons file page of the parent 'Roland Dumas, François Mitterrand and Gianni De Michelis in 1994.jpg' (preparer).

Commons API record of the same author's sibling 'Gianni De Michelis, Ugo Bergamo and François Mitterand.jpg' (uploaded 2019-11-27T14:34:20Z, date 1994, described as showing 'the Mayor of Venice Ugo Bergamo', categorised 'François Mitterrand in 1984'); fetched by the assembler to pin the date conflict.

likeness_references.date_precision: The author, Gorup de Besanez, dates the photograph only to the year 1994, and that statement is not independently confirmed. The parent is a Nikon LS-5000 film scan digitised in 2019. It also shows Roland Dumas (foreign minister until March 1993) and Gianni De Michelis (foreign minister until June 1992). The author's sibling frame from the same scan session, also dated 1994 and located 'venezia', names 'the Mayor of Venice Ugo Bergamo' (mayor 1990-1993 per it.wikipedia, as reported by the independent verifier), and Commons files that sibling under 'François Mitterrand in 1984'. The scene is therefore probably from about 1990 to 1993. likeness_references.age_gap_note: Inside the window (2008-11-29 to 2012-09-01): about 1.3 years after the start and 2.5 years before the end. She is 59 in the photograph and 58 to 62 across the window (born 8 August 1950, general knowledge). Full body, trousers and shoes are artistic extensions of a half-length photograph.

access_limits: Wikimedia Commons returned HTTP 429 several times during preparation (shared IP with parallel agents). Requests were made one at a time with back-offs of 30 to 200 seconds; nothing was bypassed.
europarl.europa.eu answered the Fabius verifier with HTTP 202, an apparent bot challenge; it was not bypassed.
shaimiev.tatarstan.ru was unreachable (connect timeout) for the Juppé verifier and the Wayback Machine was offline.

The assembler made three further single requests on 2026-10-01 (Commons file history for the Juppé file, Commons metadata for the Mitterrand sibling frame, the EC Audiovisual record for the Jospin photograph); all returned HTTP 200.
source_ledger.not_listed: HTTP response header captures in the scratch folders (for example henri_emmanuelli/hdr3.txt, martine_aubry/*.headers and francois_hollande/tmp/*.headers) contain the client IP address and GeoIP cookies. They are deliberately not listed, hashed, quoted or copied. Search scratch files, candidate downloads and view crops made by the preparers are also not ledgered; rejected candidates retained as alternates are cited with their sha256 where relevant.
